explanations.Jupiter Symphony: Mozart's Symphony No 41, nicknamed the Jupiter.
explanations.Eroica: Beethoven's Symphony No 3, titled the Eroica.
explanations.Pathetique: Tchaikovsky's Symphony No 6, known as the Pathétique.
explanations.Clarinet Concerto: Mozart's concerto in A major, written for the clarinettist Anton Stadler.
explanations.Emperor Concerto: Beethoven's Piano Concerto No 5, called the Emperor in English.
explanations.Piano Concerto No 1: Tchaikovsky's first piano concerto, in B flat minor.
explanations.The Magic Flute: Mozart's opera in two acts, to a libretto by Emanuel Schikaneder.
explanations.The Queen of Spades: Tchaikovsky's opera in three acts, after a story by Pushkin.

sources.excerpt: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart completed his Symphony No. 41 in C major, K. 551, on 10 August 1788.
The work is nicknamed the Jupiter Symphony, probably coined by the impresario Johann Peter Salomon.
The Symphony No. 3 in E♭ major, Op. 55, titled as the Eroica Symphony, is a symphony in four movements by Ludwig van Beethoven.
The Symphony No. 6 in B minor, Op. 74, also known as the Pathétique Symphony, is Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky's final completed symphony, written between February and August 1893.
Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart's Clarinet Concerto in A major, K. 622, was completed in October 1791 for the clarinettist Anton Stadler.
The Piano Concerto No. 5 in E♭ major, Op. 73, known as the Emperor Concerto in English-speaking countries, is a piano concerto composed by Ludwig van Beethoven.
The Piano Concerto No. 1 in B♭ minor, Op. 23, was composed by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky between November 1874 and February 1875.
The Magic Flute, K. 620, is an opera in two acts by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart to a German libretto by Emanuel Schikaneder.
Fidelio, originally titled Leonore, oder Der Triumph der ehelichen Liebe, Op. 72, is the sole opera by German composer Ludwig van Beethoven.

The Queen of Spades or Pique Dame, Op. 68 is an opera in three acts by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky to a Russian libretto by the composer's brother Modest Tchaikovsky, based on the 1834 novella of the same name by Alexander Pushkin, but with a dramatically altered plot.

editorNotes: Piano Concerto No 1 is the overlap and the point of the puzzle: Mozart, Beethoven and Tchaikovsky each wrote a first piano concerto, so the tile honestly fits all three concerto cells. It is pinned to Tchaikovsky by elimination, because the Clarinet Concerto belongs to Mozart alone, Beethoven and Tchaikovsky having written none, and the Emperor Concerto is Beethoven's fifth. That leaves only the Tchaikovsky concerto cell free, so the matching is single. The eight other tiles fit one cell each. Pathetique is worth a second look, since Beethoven's Piano Sonata No 8 carries the same nickname, but a sonata is neither symphony, concerto nor opera, so no second cell opens. Eroica names Beethoven's third symphony and nothing else in the grid; Beethoven also wrote Eroica Variations, again not one of these three forms. Jupiter Symphony is Mozart's alone. Fidelio was Beethoven's only opera, and Beethoven wrote no concerto for clarinet, so the two Beethoven cells cannot swap. The Queen of Spades is Tchaikovsky's opera, and though Pushkin's story of that name came first, the tile is the opera. Numbers are written without full stops, as No 1 and No 41, to keep the tiles clean and inside the length limit.
